newsitem.title: GERMANY: Adidas to sponsor 98 soccer World Cup.
newsitem.headline: Adidas to sponsor 98 soccer World Cup.

text.p: Adidas AG, in a move confirming it is back as a top sportswear brand, said on Tuesday it had bought the rights to be an official sponsor of the 1998 soccer World Cup and also acquired global licensing rights for the event.

Adidas, best known for its three-stripe logo, said the deal makes it the first worldwide sportwear maker ever to obtain exclusive rights to soccer's world championship, which will be held during the summer of 1998 in France.
"Adidas is proud to be the first sports equipment maker to join the circle of official sponsors of the soccer world championship," Adidas chief executive Robert Louis-Dreyfus said in a statement.
Adidas would not say how much it paid for the rights to the world soccer body FIFA and Japan's Sony Corp., which has the sole global merchandising rights to the event.

But similar four-year rights for the Atlanta Olympics and the 1998 Winter Olympics in Nagano, Japan, which are considered the only sports events of a larger scale than soccer's World Cup, cost each global sponsor about $40 million.

The deal marks the return of Adidas back into the ring as a global sportswear maker against U.S. rivals Nike Inc and Reebok, which have been trying to make inroads into Adidas' lucrative European markets and also into soccer.

Louis-Dreyfus, a former chief executive at advertising agency Saatchi & Saatchi, gave Adidas new life after he led an investor group that bought the group after it nearly went bankrupt under the control of French businessman Bernard Tapie.

In addition to slashing staff and cutting production in France and Germany in favour of Asia, Louis-Dreyfus boosted spending on top global events such as the Atlanta Olympics and last summer's European soccer championship to boost sales.
Adidas shares jumped on news of the World Cup deal, rising to a new record high at 145 marks before ending the bourse session in Frankfurt up 1.40 marks at 143.40 marks.
"This is one sign that Adidas is back in the world market," said adidas spokesman Peter Csanadi.
"It is a big honour for us to be a sponsor because we have a long history in soccer. But it is also an enormous business opportunity," Csanadi said.
Adidas said the first licensed products related to the soccer event would be launched in France a few months before the December holiday season.
An official football for the World Cup would be presented in Marseille in December 1997 and Adidas will also provide uniforms for about 12,000 World Cup staff and helpers.
Adidas already supplies the official football and referee equipment for many FIFA games.

In the more lucrative area, adidas will have the global rights to use the World Cup logo on its products, particularly on shirts, balls and other sportswear items that experts say add up to several millions of marks in sales.
Adidas has long been a major player in the global soccer industry since it was founded more than 70 years ago by Adi Dassler in the south German town of Herzogenaurach.

The sportswear maker is the official sponsor of the German Argentinian, Spanish and French national soccer teams and also top European clubs such as Bayern Munich, Olympique de Marsaille, Newcastle United and Glascow Rangers.
Some top international players endorsed by Adidas include Paul Gascoigne, Matthias Sammer and Marcel Desailly.
